citation: Kinzie, Juliette A. M. Wau-Bun: The 'Early Day' in the North-West. New York: Derby & Jackson, 1856.
author: Juliette Augusta Magill Kinzie
locator: ch. XVII, 'Chicago in 1831'; first 1856 edition printed pp. 210/221 (1812 baggage wagons); ch. XXIII 'Second Sight—Hickory Creek', p. 297 (1831 light dearborn wagon), and ch. XXIV 'Return to Fort Winnebago', p. 302 (pair of travelling horses), IA waubunearlydayin00kinz_0 scans 0309/0314
note: The only near-contemporary descriptive text for the Wolf Point buildings. Load-bearing for the Sauganash: 'a pretentious white two-story building, with bright-blue wooden shutters, the admiration of all the little circle at Wolf Point.' Written 25 years after the events and describing 1831, not 1835 — hence tier 2 and the describes_date field. Also the source for the Indian Agency house ('logs hewed and squared, with a centre, two wings') and for the Wolf Point name deriving from an Indian resident called Moa-way, 'the Wolf'. Vehicle use: p297 names Kercheval bringing a light dearborn wagon from Detroit, purchased by John Harris Kinzie for his mother and nephew; p302 names a pair of travelling horses. This is the1831 journey, not1812 and not proof the same wagon stood in Chicago1835. Maker, measurements, roof/curtains, paint and exact1835 placement are not supplied.
